title: SOS: Score-based Oversampling for Tabular Data

problem.claim: Imbalanced classes can lead to sub-optimal training outcomes, motivating oversampling of minor classes.

gap.claim: Existing score-based generative models are primarily described for fake-image generation, while score-based tabular-data oversampling is presented as an unmet need.

contributions.claim: A score-based method is customized for generating fake tabular data and oversampling minor classes.
A redesigned score network is provided for processing tabular data.
The method provides two generation options and a fine-tuning method intended to enhance oversampling quality.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In experiments with 6 datasets and 10 baselines, the authors report that their method outperforms other oversampling methods in all cases.

narrative_sequence.summary: Score-based generative models have achieved success in generating fake images and are reported to surpass GANs and VAEs.
The work targets oversampling of minor classes in tabular data because class imbalance can produce sub-optimal training outcomes.
The authors customize score-based generation for tabular data, redesign the score network, and provide two generation options.
A fine-tuning method is defined to further enhance oversampling quality.
Experiments across 6 datasets and 10 baselines are reported to favor the proposed method in all cases.

source_observation.claim: The method adapts score-based generation to tabular data through a redesigned score network and alternative generation procedures.

interpretation.claim: Successful transfer of a generative approach across data modalities may require changes to both the model representation and generation procedure.

application.claim: When adapting generative models to structured data, assess whether the network architecture and sampling policy fit the data modality.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that these adaptations are necessary or effective for modalities beyond the reported tabular-data setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the dataset identities, evaluation metrics, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the score network, generation options, or fine-tuning method.
The abstract does not provide independently verified results or statistical uncertainty.
